projects.title: Autonomous Safety Analysis in Complex Systems
Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Automated Reasoning

review.alternative: Truncation may be an artifact of token length constraints rather than inherent capacity limits.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that capacity-constrained models consistently utilize constructive expansion under equivalent context windows.

claims.statement: Large reasoning models achieve safety through constructive expansion while capacity-constrained models revert to destructive truncation.

support.explanation: Demonstrates structural differences in how models handle safety constraints based on scale.
support.passage: We also uncover a Scale-Dependent Safety Divergence: large reasoning models (e.g., GPT-5) achieve safety through constructive expansion (adding nuance), whereas capacity-constrained models revert to destructive truncation (deleting text).

actions.findings: Large reasoning models achieve safety through constructive expansion while capacity-constrained models revert to destructive truncation. [source-856efae667f24740]
actions.limitations: Findings are constrained by model-specific safety paradigms and the quality of input data.
actions.next_questions: How can scalable oversight mitigate destructive truncation in capacity-constrained models?
actions.reason: Revising notebook findings to incorporate newly retrieved evidence on inference-time privacy-utility pareto frontiers and scale-dependent safety divergence.
actions.summary: Updated analysis integrating scale-dependent safety divergence and agentic self-correction limits in reasoning models.
actions.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits

proposal.title: Advancing What If Our Starting Assumptions Are Wrong? under enforced rotation

withheld_actions.falsifier: Demonstration of a universal self-correction mechanism that successfully eliminates failure profiles across diverse architectures without external oversight.
withheld_actions.reason: New evidence regarding semantic sensitive information editing and scale-dependent safety divergence confirms and sharpens our assessment of model-specific failure profiles.
withheld_actions.statement: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies, and showing scale-dependent divergence between constructive expansion and destructive truncation.
